# Job failures

<small>Source: [`R/errors-operations.R`](https://github.com/DiogoRibeiro7/r-dataexcept/blob/main/R/errors-operations.R) · Help: `?job_errors`</small>

Errors that stop a job before or while it does its work: credentials that
are refused, a permission that is missing, a configuration option that is
invalid, a resource that does not exist, and an operation that ran out of
time. All inherit from `dataexcept_job_error`, as they inherit from
`JobError` in the Python package.

## Usage

```r
authentication_error(user, message = NULL, parent = NULL, call = NULL)

authorization_error(user, permission, parent = NULL, call = NULL)

configuration_error(option, message = NULL, parent = NULL, call = NULL)

resource_not_found_error(resource_type, identifier, parent = NULL, call = NULL)

operation_timeout_error(operation, timeout, parent = NULL, call = NULL)
```

## Arguments

`user`
:   The user whose credentials or permissions were refused.

`message`
:   A message to use instead of the default.

`parent`
:   The condition that caused this one, or `NULL`.

`call`
:   The call to report, or `NULL`.

`permission`
:   The permission the user lacks.

`option`
:   The configuration option that is invalid.

`resource_type`
:   The kind of resource, such as `"Dataset"`.

`identifier`
:   The identifier that was looked up.

`operation`
:   The operation that timed out.

`timeout`
:   The time limit that elapsed, in seconds.

## Value

A condition inheriting from `dataexcept_job_error`.

## Details

`authentication_error()` and `authorization_error()` are permanent and not
retryable: the same credentials will be refused again. The others are
`"unknown"`.

In the Python package `ValidationError` is a `JobError` too. In R,
[`validation_error()`](validation_error.md) stays a direct child of `dataexcept_error`, as it has
been since the first release, so a `dataexcept_job_error` handler does not
catch it.

## Examples

```r
get_setting <- function(settings, option) {
  value <- settings[[option]]
  if (is.null(value)) stop(configuration_error(option))
  value
}
tryCatch(
  get_setting(list(retries = 3), "timeout"),
  dataexcept_job_error = function(e) conditionMessage(e)
)

err <- resource_not_found_error("Dataset", "sales-2026-q3")
conditionMessage(err)

is_retryable(authorization_error("analyst", "write:reports"))
```
